operation: Existing Show editor on the v2 backing at 1440x900 with reduced motion; fresh Installation Shows seeded through /api/shows and stored as v2. Re-captured at the duplicate-repair tip. Capture 1: two Clips on one Layer, no Transition (TestPattern1D 0-30 s, CometLoom 30-60 s on layer:zone-1:main); CometLoom dropped a quarter of the way in, over TestPattern1D. The clip-temporal owner refuses the overlap: CometLoom shows the red 'Space taken' label and the timeline role=status reads 'Clips on one Layer cannot overlap.'. 1.5 s later the stored v2 record is unchanged (updatedAt 1790223659337 before and after; both Clips' id, start, duration and Layer identical). Capture 2 (Show d6fddd6f-7352-4c91-9b69-f2c790e892d7): the default Installation Show with its converted crossfade Transition (30000-31999 ms), plus a second empty Layer added through Add > Layer because the Transition's own control covers its Layer. A double-click on that Layer at 31000 ms refuses the add: the timeline role=status reads 'A Clip cannot start inside a Transition.', no Clip label, no add dialog, stored updatedAt unchanged. The status line is screen-reader only; the proof script removed its sr-only class for the capture alone and drew it bottom-left. Capture 3 (Show 3e19ea92-e64d-4966-9e6e-2725928547bc): the same two-Clip Show. An Alt-drag of CometLoom starts; mid-drag the page's store adopts a record whose Show End is extended to 90 s at a new revision (standing in for another tab or the agent). The timeline redraws against 90 s, so the copy dropped at the lane's end clamps past the drag's captured 60 s Show End; the duplicate check refuses the preview (no preview painted), and the drag ends with no drop. The release reports the refusal as a race: CometLoom shows 'Show changed', the status reads 'The Show changed; try again.', no 'Space taken' appears, and the stored record is unchanged (updatedAt 1790223659335 before and after; both Clips identical). A plain Alt-duplicate cannot reach this refusal: both drag paths clamp the copy inside the current Show End.
